subject: reply-draft-henri-PR29-issue24-audit-use-case

metrics.subject_line: Re: [Audit] Support for PR #29, and the case for carrying issue #24 point 2 with it
metrics.draft_text:
Henri,

CSOAI supports merging PR #29 with issue #24, point 2 carried alongside it.

Our draft-csoai-audit-use-case-00 (ticket rt5.ietf.org #57030, still processing in the queue) covers the receipt shape for actions that proceeded: subject identifier, axis, Wilson 95% CI accuracy, n>=30 sample, run identifier, harness + grader version, prompt digest, raw response digest, regulatory crosswalk, Ed25519 signature over canonicalized JSON body, Merkle inclusion via /api/proof, Rekor witness, OpenTimestamps Bitcoin anchor.

Your observation is correct that this is incomplete without a place for records that describe a non-event. A refusal produces one record and no counterpart. If the data model offers only correlation shapes, then 'stopped at the boundary' and 'no record exists' read the same to an auditor.

We propose adding a section to our draft covering decision-time decline records, citing draft-sirkkavaara-vaara-receipt as informational reference for the envelope shape. The amendment is additive, not replacement: the existing receipt shape remains unchanged, and decline records become a recognised sibling.

The three independent threads that raised this property — your 12 September message, Steven Mih's issue #24 filed in Vienna, Sumit Ahuja's 8 and 11 September messages — were answered separately because no one reading the repository could see the others. The audit@ietf.org archive should make the convergence visible. That is a structural fix, not a working-group one.

Nicholas Templeman
CSOAI Ltd (UK 16939677)
draft-csoai-audit-use-case-00 author
